question.text: Consider two containers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> containing monoatomic gases at the same Pressure <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>P</mi></mfenced></math>, Volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>V</mi></mfenced></math> and Temperature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>T</mi></mfenced></math>. The gas in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is compressed isothermally to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math> of its original volume while the gas in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> is compressed adiabatically to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math> of its original volume. The ratio of final pressure of gas in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> to that of gas in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is

solution.text:
In an isothermal process the temperature is constant.

PV=nRT

So, it can be written that 

PV=PAV8⇒PA=8P

In an adiabatic process,

PVγ=constant

γ for monoatomic gas is 53

So, it can be written

PBP=VV853⇒PB=32P

Thus, the ratio of the pressures is 

PBPA=32P8P=4
